body:
Maps can now carry author-defined terrain using the existing property schema and shipped appearances. The editor imports strict JSON definitions atomically, preserves custom IDs on reimport, and exposes a scrollable palette in desktop and phone layouts. Maps, saves and replays embed resolved definitions, so recipients need no local terrain JSON.

The immutable per-map registry preserves built-in IDs and behavior. Compact property and movement profiles share equivalent definitions; map-local summaries keep unused definitions out of gradient setup. Scenes and background jobs capture registry snapshots. Prepared scalar/SSE2/NEON kernels select validated 64/128/256-bucket variants outside inner loops. Detailed rendering uses the shared material compositor: scenes cache shipped appearance IDs, aliases resolve to the same material, and render caches bind registry and asset identity. Import and persistence avoid duplicate expanded JSON trees.

Persistence advances to format 136 and network protocol 56; the save floor remains 58 and replay floor remains 134. SIM_REVISION advances to 19 with a regenerated golden record. Built-in-only checksum contributions are unchanged; custom registries contribute a canonical cached digest. Frozen serialized presentation fields remain separate from the material catalog. Custom terrain uses full-tile presentation, so boundaries can differ intentionally from legacy corner tiles. Built-in game behavior is intended to remain unchanged.

Two independent reviews addressed registry string ownership, unsafe queue selection, redundant building-search branches, appearance sharing, picker behavior and UI scaling/translations. Regression tests exercise actual background-job publication and desktop/phone file-selection, import, retry, palette and save/load flows. Development, material-authoring and map-authoring guides explain ownership, index domains, queue constraints and reimport behavior.

Current master `d7e3af8ec` was integrated after resolving real conflicts with the material renderer. Final validation at `ea5407b22` on Linux x86-64 / GCC15:

- **87 affected engine cases**, **818 headless unit cases**, all **18 display unit cases**, and **56 UI/rendering cases** passed.
- Old format-135 replay and embedded custom verifier replay pass stored per-tick checksum checks. Custom LAN transfer, shared-map validation and pending-gradient restoration pass.
- Scalar and emulated ARM64/NEON registry/kernel tests each pass **251 assertions in eight cases**. Full ARM64 engine determinism remains separate coverage.
- Scene-boundary, translation, pinned asset-packaging, browser-packaging, CI-policy, web-asset and terrain asset compiler checks pass (one web test skipped). Cheap hosted checks pass; expensive platform jobs were skipped.

**Remaining qualification.** Ten randomized paired renderer rounds at 7/259/1,024/16,384 definitions have similar median frame CPU (about 4 ms), but high host load produces wide confidence intervals. These results are inconclusive. Full Windows/native ARM64/browser-WASM engine checksum comparisons, quiet-machine full-match/kernel measurements, additional representative match workloads and GPU performance remain outstanding. Earlier pre-integration performance results are labeled with their actual revisions in the evidence; they are not claims about the final material renderer.

[Final review evidence and limitations](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/blob/4f5c44da8da4008caa15f7adf30ff986c4472d91/artifacts/runtime-terrain-master-evidence/README.md) includes exact revisions/base, commands, dependency/toolchain metadata, test logs and inventories, replay checksums, raw renderer CPU/wall/RSS measurements, and desktop/phone screenshots. It links the previous review findings, broader earlier engine run, original fixtures and before/after full-match/kernel measurements. Evidence is published on a dedicated branch, separately from product documentation.

Local validation evidence for tested head `ad8406ed6` against pinned base `dbc6253427edc1ca71227ec91a8cd9ab66b5d326`:

[Evidence index, commands, environment, coverage rationale and limitations](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/blob/96a3f949bf4f4aeca3ea521d9b940a71d5fa999a/artifacts/runtime-terrain-evidence/README.md) · [Download logs, fixtures and measurements](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/raw/96a3f949bf4f4aeca3ea521d9b940a71d5fa999a/artifacts/runtime-terrain-evidence/evidence.tar.gz) · [SHA-256](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/blob/96a3f949bf4f4aeca3ea521d9b940a71d5fa999a/artifacts/runtime-terrain-evidence/archive.sha256)

Linux x86-64 / Threadripper 2950X / GCC 15 / release `-O3`; identical dependency prefix and build flags for the feature/base. Native engine: 669 passed, zero failed, 101 skipped. Native headless units: 816 passed, 17 display cases skipped. Focused software/OpenGL/editor/preview coverage: 10 passed. Scalar and QEMU ARM64/NEON registry/kernel oracle: 218 assertions each. Final-head old local replay and custom network verifier replay validate their stored per-tick checksums. JUnit lists individual cases and omissions; the bundle includes LAN-distributed custom maps, match records, saves, replays and checksum traces.

The final randomized paired measurements include separate CPU/wall time, RSS, commands, shuffle seeds and warm-ups: 10 complete-match repetitions per variant and 15 terrain-kernel rounds. All match variants finish at 17,090 ticks with identical team outcomes. Native built-in CPU mean paired difference is -1.28% (bootstrap interval -3.41% to +0.71%); custom equivalent kernel CPU is approximately 13–15% lower. Shared-host noise means this does **not** satisfy the quiet-machine acceptance requirement.

Outstanding: full Windows/native ARM64/browser-WASM engine determinism, additional full-match workloads, quiet-machine performance qualification, GPU performance, and review/optimization of maximum-size registry cost. At 16,384 definitions, software render CPU/frame is +24.76% versus seven definitions; peak RSS is about 300 MiB headless and 556 MiB in the renderer. QEMU kernel equality is not whole-engine platform coverage. Draft status is intentional; no claim of completed qualification or hosted CI verification.

[Desktop palette screenshot](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/blob/96a3f949bf4f4aeca3ea521d9b940a71d5fa999a/artifacts/runtime-terrain-evidence/screenshots/terrain-palette-desktop.png) · [Phone palette screenshot](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/blob/96a3f949bf4f4aeca3ea521d9b940a71d5fa999a/artifacts/runtime-terrain-evidence/screenshots/terrain-palette-phone.png)

Completed two independent reviews, followed by a second review of the integrated fixes. No additional blocking correctness findings remained. The review fixed unsafe registry copying/borrowed strings, validates ring capacity before field mutation, removes dead search code, deduplicates complete visual profiles, reduces JSON peak memory, and strengthens real editor/job-pipeline tests. Documentation, comments, translations and scene dependency boundaries were cleaned up with the implementation.

Tested head: `7afc0e1c24a65c2610277dff34dbaf3425c65cb6`; integrated base: `dbc6253427edc1ca71227ec91a8cd9ab66b5d326`. Current master was fetched; subsequent music-buffer changes did not overlap this work. Environment: Linux x86-64, Threadripper 2950X, GCC 15.2, release `-O3`, freshly rebuilt repository-pinned SDL dependencies. Both benchmark binaries used the same dependency bundle.

The broad cleanup run at `ba739d5d7` passed 671 engine cases. Final scene-boundary integration passed 67 affected engine cases, 818 headless units, 40 UI/rendering cases and both old/custom replay checks. Scalar and QEMU ARM64/NEON tests each passed 252 assertions; their sources did not change during the final scene integration. Boundary and translation checks passed. Headless/default skips are recorded in JUnit. This does not claim full Windows, native ARM64 or WASM engine checksum coverage.

[Published review evidence](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/blob/910ac69c6af6ce1afa8b804860ffcb02423f1421/artifacts/runtime-terrain-review-evidence/README.md) contains the findings/dispositions, exact command arrays, tested revisions and dependency manifests, JUnit/logs, replay/map/save fixtures, checksums, screenshots and raw paired benchmark data. The downloadable archive has a SHA-256 checksum and an internal file manifest. The PR body now reflects these results.

Ten randomized paired measurements show maximum-registry headless peak RSS down 58.84%, software frame CPU down 24.19%, and renderer RSS down 34.71%. Setup CPU rose 16.35%. Built-in match CPU measured +0.26% (95% interval -0.69% to +1.27%); maximum-registry match CPU measured +1.80% (-0.38% to +3.85%). Shared-host noise means strict performance qualification is still inconclusive. The PR remains draft for quiet-machine qualification, broader match/GPU workloads and full platform determinism coverage. Cheap hosted checks passed; they do not substitute for these outstanding checks.

Final integration refresh: `ea5407b22fb00bbf223b283bd5c7c78d098f2177`, based on newly integrated master `d7e3af8ec3e58455a55a55e3ce347df0ec930115`.

The final mergeability check caught master #795 after the earlier review evidence was published. Both reviewers returned to resolve that real overlap. Custom terrain now uses the shared material compositor with compact scene appearance IDs. Obsolete visual-profile storage was removed; resolved save fields/digests remain frozen. A silent automatic-merge error in custom-ID frame validation was corrected. The branch is now mergeable.

Final Linux x86-64 GCC15 release validation passes: 87 affected engine cases, 818 headless units, all 18 display units, 56 UI/rendering cases, both old/custom replay checksum checks, and 251 scalar plus 251 QEMU ARM64/NEON assertions. Boundary, translation and asset/package/policy checks also pass. The earlier 671-case broad engine run remains identified at its earlier cleanup revision; it is not relabeled as a final-head run.

[Published final evidence](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/blob/4f5c44da8da4008caa15f7adf30ff986c4472d91/artifacts/runtime-terrain-master-evidence/README.md) contains exact commands, revision/base/environment/dependency metadata, successful build/test logs, JUnit inventories, replay verification, raw renderer measurements and screenshots, plus a downloadable archive and SHA-256 manifest. The PR body has been rewritten around the integrated architecture and current results.

Ten randomized renderer rounds are complete, but host load of roughly 25–37 gives wide intervals; performance qualification remains inconclusive. The earlier 24% frame-CPU and 59% headless-memory improvements refer to `7afc0e1c2` versus `ad8406ed6`, not the final material renderer. Final full-match before/after timing was not repeated after this renderer integration. Full platform engine determinism, quiet-machine timing, broader matches and GPU performance remain open, so this PR stays draft. Cheap hosted success does not cover those gaps.

title: Add runtime terrain definitions with compiled movement profiles
